Cyberpunk 2 Won’t Live in Grand Theft Auto 6’s Shadow, and CDPR Shares New Details About Its Highly Anticipated Open-World Game
items.summary: CD Projekt RED is actively developing Cyberpunk 2, codenamed Project Orion, despite the industry's focus on Grand Theft Auto 6. The studio confirmed that production is on schedule and plans to expand its workforce to 320 employees by next year, with the game expected to build on its predecessor's concepts. While the gaming community remains largely in the dark about specifics, the development team is optimistic about the project's progress, though comparisons to Rockstar Games' recent success are inevitable.

window.__runDeferredScript({"id":"custom-script-8ccaa8a7","src":"https://t.seedtag.com/t/4204-4423-01.js","strategy":"userInteraction","attributes":{}}); WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW:

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the game of the moment, and many already consider it one of the greatest titles in history. Following this historic release, it’s clearer than ever that the rest of the industry will have a hard time impressing players. Despite the comparisons, CDPR doesn’t plan to remain in Rockstar Games’ shadow and has shared new information about the development of Cyberpunk 2 .

The sequel to the successful, but also controversial, sci-fi RPG is in full production, even though The Witcher 4 is currently CD Projekt RED’s top priority. In this regard, the Polish studio has revealed new details about the development of its 2020 game’s sequel.

It was in late 2022 when CD Projekt RED officially confirmed the sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 , which is currently known by its codename, Project Orion. Several years have passed since then, and most details about its mechanics and story remain a mystery.

Even so, we know that the developers are still hard at work on the project. The topic came up again during the company’s latest investor meeting, where CDPR revealed its plans for Cyberpunk 2 . Fans will still have to be patient, but there is some encouraging news.

During its financial results presentation, the Polish studio confirmed that production on the sci-fi game is ongoing and progressing according to schedule. The company also stated that the team is satisfied with the game’s current state.

Unfortunately, the possible date for its official public reveal remains unknown. Nevertheless, these statements make it clear that the project is making good progress behind the scenes.

“We are making good progress with Cyberpunk 2. We are satisfied with the current state, but it is still too early to give a specific date and plan when we will begin full-scale production,” said Karolina Gnaś, CDPR’s Vice President of Investor Relations, during the meeting.

CD Projekt RED also revealed that it plans to expand its workforce to strengthen development of the next installment in the franchise . An estimated 200 developers are currently working on the ambitious project, and the goal is to reach 320 employees by the end of next year.

For comparison, around 513 people are actively working on The Witcher 4 , which, according to reports, may not launch until 2028. Overall, the European company has approximately 1,051 employees, up from the 1,045 it had in July this year.

Very little is known about Cyberpunk 2 , but it is expected to expand on the original game’s concept. Mike Pondsmith, the franchise’s creator, hinted at the possibility of the game taking place in two cities: Night City and an exaggerated parody of Chicago. Likewise, members of the modding community are believed to be involved in production.

Whatever the case, one thing is certain: CD Projekt RED will face comparisons with Rockstar Games. Following the success of Grand Theft Auto 6 , Igor Sarzyński, director of Cyberpunk 2 , joked about canceling the project and said that the overwhelmingly positive reception of Take-Two Interactive’s title had left the development team feeling depressed.

“The GTA 6-induced open-world game development depression is real. It’s probably the greatest artistic achievement in history given its scale, density, coherence, and a technological and creative miracle,” the creative director commented.

Furthermore, CDPR’s investors are adding to that pressure. During the financial results meeting, one shareholder asked the Polish team how the upcoming The Witcher 4 would compare with GTA 6 . In response, Michał Nowakowski, CDPR’s co-CEO, said the company is focused on its own projects.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Sequel Progress is “Good” So Far, “Still Too Early” To Reveal More Details
items.summary: CD Projekt RED's Karolina Gnaś also spoke about how the company is working on many projects in parallel, like The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2.
items.content:
CD Projekt RED has confirmed in its recent earnings call that the sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 is still quite some time away. The company’s VP of strategy and investor relations, Karolina Gnaś, also noted that progress on the project has been “good” so far, and that the company has been generally happy about the development process so far.

However, “it’s still too early to give a specific date and plan on when we will move onto full production,” said Gnaś during the call. In the meantime, CD Projekt RED isn’t slowing down its plans to further grow its headcount to help with development, with plans to have 200 developers on the project by the end of the year, and 320 by the end of 2027.

It is worth noting that CD Projekt RED is also yet to showcase its sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 in any way. The company is likely busier with its work on The Witcher 4 for now, which is quite a bit further along in development. Gnaś went on to note that the company is concurrently working on “several” projects right now.

“At the moment, the CD Projekt Red studio is working in parallel on several productions (also in collaboration with external development teams) and supporting products, which is expected to translate into shorter intervals between the releases of subsequent titles in the future.”

During the same earnings call, co-CEO Michał Nowakowski said that the recent release of Grand Theft Auto 6 hasn’t really brought about any changes in CD Projekt RED’s plans for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 , especially when it comes to the company’s ambitions .

“Is seeing GTA 6 launch making us make the games more expensive? We have certain ambitions when it comes to Witcher [ 4 ] and Cyberpunk 2 ; they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6 . If anything happened as a result of GTA 6 , it’s [that it’s] always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done, and that’s for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers.”

He also spoke about how, while the two projects aren’t “budget-driven developments”, the company still wants to be careful about how it spends its money on them.

“I’m not saying we don’t care about the budgets: we do, and I’m pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well. But you cannot make games like that having in mind ‘this is the fixed number of money I want to spend and that’s it, otherwise I’m gone’.

“They’re ambition-driven developments, and money’s important – the budgets are not indefinite; that’s not what we’re saying. But the philosophy is, like I said, and honestly that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6 ‘s release; it has just always been like that.”

Currently, while CD Projekt RED has showcased The Witcher 4 with a couple of trailers over the last few years, the company still hasn’t confirmed a release window for the RPG. However, recent reports have indicated that it might come out before April 30th, 2028 .

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 sequel lands surprise update as Project Orion launch window grows more visible
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2's launch date may have been narrowed down...
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2 now has an approximate launch window thanks to a new CD Projekt Red investors call.

The Cyberpunk 2077 sequel, currently known as Cyberpunk 2 or Project Orion, is reportedly shifting into full-production soon. This gives us a good idea of when it’ll launch.

It honestly feels like it’s too early to be talking about another Cyberpunk game , as it does months of hard work and post-launch support to get the current game to its now-excellent state.

On top of that CD Projekt Red’s next game is confirmed to be The Witcher IV , which is expected to launch in 2028 and is apparently borrowing something from Grand Theft Auto VI…

However, in a new investor’s call CD Projekt Red’s Vice President CD Karolina Gnaś confirmed the studio will be increasing its staff next year, and that can only mean one thing…

Using The Witcher IV we can somewhat gleam how long it’ll take for CD Projekt Red to finish its next Cyberpunk game, but don’t take this as the gospel truth as there’s a little bit of speculation involved – and a lot of wishful thinking.

The Witcher IV entered full-production in 2024, and is now set for launch sometime in 2028 provided there are no delays.

At the earliest, Cyberpunk 2 could enter production sometime in 2027, and based on CD Projekt Red’s previous production windows we could see it launch as soon as 2031.

The more likely scenario is it enters production either next year, or early 2028, and then launches around 2032/2033, but we’re optimists here at GAMINGbible.

Despite being widely different IPs and genres both The Witcher IV and Cyberpunk 2 are both intended to be grand open-world games, so it’s safe to say their development cycles won’t be all that different from one another. Cyberpunk 2 might need a little extra time so the studio doesn’t repeat the mistakes of the past…

Again, take all of this with a pinch of salt, but CD Projekt Red bolstering its workforce next year is a pretty good indication that new projects are being set in motion, and some of those workers are actually modders the studio head-hunted.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2 director calls GTA 6 a “creative miracle” and says his own sequel will have a different flavour
items.summary: GTA 6 has impressed the creative director of Cyberpunk 2, and he is not being subtle about it. Igor Sarzyński called Rockstar’s game a “technological and
items.content:
This article needs JavaScript to display. Please turn on JavaScript in your browser and reload the page. GTA 6 has impressed the creative director of Cyberpunk 2 , and he is not being subtle about it. Igor Sarzyński called Rockstar’s game a “technological and creative miracle” while praising its scale, density and attention to detail.

He also joked that his own game was cancelled after playing it. To be clear, that was a joke, not a cancellation announcement. In a follow-up, Sarzyński said his team is making something of its own with a different flavour.

The comments offer an interesting glimpse of how another open-world developer sees a game that has dominated the conversation since its launch. They do not reveal a release date or finished features for Cyberpunk 2 .

Rockstar Games artwork for GTA 6. Image: Rockstar Games

In a Bluesky post on November 21 , Sarzyński described Rockstar’s game as “probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history” and pointed to its scale, density, coherence and thoughtfulness.

He then wrote that Cyberpunk 2 was cancelled and joked about sweeping leaves in his garden. That playful line should not be mistaken for an update on the game’s production status.

In a later post , he put the comparison in context. “GTA is impressive in a way all great art is,” he wrote, adding that it expands what is possible and calling it a captivating vision.

He is not the only person at CD Projekt to praise Rockstar’s release. As we reported separately , joint CEO Michał Nowakowski also congratulated the studio and called the game a masterpiece.

An image from Cyberpunk 2077, not Cyberpunk 2. Image: CD Projekt RED / Steam

Sarzyński’s follow-up makes the distinction worth remembering. His comment about a different flavour is a broad statement of intent, not a list of mechanics or a promise about the final sequel.

GTA 6 and Cyberpunk 2077 both give players large worlds to explore, but their settings and stories are quite different. It is reasonable to be curious about what developers learn from Rockstar’s work without assuming the next Cyberpunk will copy it.

Our featured image and garage screenshot come from Cyberpunk 2077 , the existing game. They are not screenshots of the unreleased sequel. The other images are official GTA 6 material from Rockstar.

The director praised the scale and detail of Rockstar’s game. Image: Rockstar Games

If you want to see the game Sarzyński was discussing, Amazon lists GTA 6 for PlayStation 5 . Check the listing before ordering: this version is a code in a box, not a game disc, and it is separate from Cyberpunk 2 .

7 Long Open-World RPGs That Take Forever to Complete
items.summary: Open-world games like Cyberpunk 2077 will keep players busy for 100 hours or more.
items.content:
Image via CD Projekt Red Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Sage Negron Published Nov 23, 2026, 7:30 PM EST Sage Negron is a freelance writer based in New York City. He has contributed to CBR in the past, as well as Looper and DualShockers. When he's not writing, he's usually playing video games or reading a good book. Sign in to your CBR account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap One of the many reasons open-world RPGs are so popular is that they can keep players busy for dozens of hours or more. Games are often on the long side even if players focus on the main story, and if players delve into optional content like side quests and collectibles, it'll keep them busy for much longer.

Games like Cyberpunk 2077 can potentially keep players busy for hundreds of hours, making them a worthwhile investment even if players buy them at full price. Best of all, many of these games have mods that expand the original experience even more, so players could potentially play and enjoy them forever.

The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind Image via Bethesda Game Studios One of the things that makes every game in the Elder Scrolls series such fun is the fact that each game allows the player to do however they please. If they want to follow the main story, they can do so. But if they want to go off and explore the world , then they will not be punished for their actions.

The third entry, Morrowind , perfectly embodies this philosophy. The open world is jam-packed with factions to meet and side quests to complete, all of which help players level up and experiment with new armor and weapons builds. Even with all of this in the base game, two expansions and even more locations and monsters to discover, making Morrowind one of the biggest games ever.

V in a car chase with police in Cyberpunk 2077 Image via CD PROJEKT RED The main narrative of Cyberpunk 2077 , which revolves around a mercenary trying to stop their death at the hands of a chip in their brain containing the memories of a former rock star, is not a long story. Players can go through all the story missions in roughly 20 hours. But exploring everything that Night City has to offer will take much longer.

There is always a new side mission for V to undertake , or a new gig that can earn them some extra cash in one of the city's many districts. And performing these tasks will allow V to purchase new weapons, vehicles, and hideouts scattered across the map. Both the main game and the Phantom Liberty expansion will keep players busy for a very long time.

Arc Hunter in Destiny 2 Image via Bungie It was recently announced that Destiny 2 would not be receiving any more content updates, leaving behind nearly a decade's worth of gameplay modes for players to experience. It's the end of an era for the MMORPG FPS game, but that doesn’t mean that new or returning players won’t have anything to do.

These open world RPGs feel like classic game titles, but they're built for the modern age of PC gaming perfectly.

With each new year, new story expansions were introduced that added new lore to the franchise, alongside new missions, raids, gear, and modes ranging from PvP to PvE. Since Destiny 2 will still remain playable for the foreseeable future, players will have plenty of time to finish everything that these expansions have to offer, which could take hundreds of hours to even scratch the surface of.

Image via Lo-Fi Games The length of time it takes to complete Kenshi depends entirely on how much time the player is willing to put into it. The real-time strategy RPG isn’t built around a traditional story. Instead, all the player has to do is survive in a post-apocalyptic world while dealing with hostile NPCs and even more hostile environmental conditions, and that is easier said than done.

Not only is leveling up the player character very time-consuming, but the world will throw everything it can at the player to stop their progress. Factions can attack the player, weather conditions can halt the progress of resource management and exploration, and getting attacked can cause players to lose their limbs. Kenshi is the start of a long and painful story of survival.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is enjoying what may very well be the single greatest media launch in history, securing over $3.7 billion in launch sales. But as Rockstar enjoys its acclaim, other developers—like Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski—are professing some anxiety about releasing their own games in a post-GTA 6 world.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle," Sarzynski said on Bluesky over the weekend, joking that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled."

That news came as a surprise to Cyberpunk 2 lead writer Anna Megill, who replied with a baffled "But wait—"

Sarzynski was, of course, just goofing. But I'm sympathetic to any game dev who might be feeling an amount of apprehension about being measured against GTA 6's success, particularly when there's a genre overlap.

In Cyberpunk 2's case, however, CD Projekt is very much in its own lane: Cyberpunk is a different thematic setting, with entirely different systems and design goals. I'd hope that any reasonable person would think comparing the two is like comparing apples and oranges—particularly when the oranges reportedly had a production budget upwards of $1 billion .

"Seriously though, I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he said. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is: It expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed."

items.title: From the Anime to the Game — Free Update Brings Edgerunners 2 Content and More to Cyberpunk 2077!
items.summary: The free Edgerunners 2 Update to Cyberpunk 2077 is available now, with content inspired by the second installment of the hit anime series now streaming on Netflix
items.content:
“Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” premiered on Netflix on October 20, bringing a whole new cast of characters to Night City for a dark, gritty ride. And now we’re bringing a little piece of that story into Cyberpunk 2077 , too! The free Edgerunners 2 Update is here, with content inspired by the anime, new ways to fight, more customization options, and plenty of other additions.

We’ve got a lot to cover, so let’s get into it. And don’t worry if you haven’t watched the new anime yet — no “Edgerunners 2” spoilers ahead!

One of the things we love about Night City is that there’s always another story unfolding somewhere. V may be central to the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , but they’re hardly the only merc in town, fighting to survive and make a name for themselves on those neon-soaked streets. Every fixer has clients, every crew has gigs to take care of, every Night City merc has their story — and sometimes, those stories collide in unexpected ways.

That’s exactly what happens in the brand-new quest introduced with the “Edgerunners 2” Update. What begins as just another gig from Wakako turns into an action-packed, high-stakes mission that sees V cross paths with Weak Kingsley, a famed Night City merc and one of the main characters of “Edgerunners 2.” We won’t spoil what happens, but during the course of this mission, V has a chance to assist Weak and his crew during a risky gig that takes place in a brand-new location: Night City Prison.

The new “Edgerunners 2” gig is more than a chance to encounter characters from the anime in the game — it serves as a prequel to the events of the series. So, play the quest before watching the anime, and you’ll have a little extra context going into Episode 1. Already seen the show? Then with this gig, you’ll get to revisit part of Weak’s story with a broader perspective of him and his crew.

And there’s even more forEdgerunnersfans in this update. For starters, you can find and equip Weak’s full outfit — vest, glasses, coat, pants, the works — and get your hands on his signature revolver, Coronation. We’ve also added a new radio station, HKGN 102.FM, featuring official tracks from both “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners” and “Edgerunners 2.” So if you’re planning to spend a few more hours cruising around Night City after watching the show, we’ve got your soundtrack covered.

What’s better than blasting your way through a warehouse full of gangoons with a revolver, dealing one headshot after another? Doing it with two revolvers, obviously.

That’s right — dual wielding is here! With the Edgerunners 2 Update, you can raise hell with a pistol or revolver in each hand. That’s a whole new vibe — and a whole new level of awesome.

But dual wielding isn’t just about looking cool. It brings a new playstyle and a fresh way to approach combat — in fact, it’s one of the most significant gameplay additions to the game’s combat since Update 2.0 introduced throwing knives. So if you’ve been looking for an excuse to shake up your fighting style, this might just be it.

Cyberware enhances your stats and abilities — but what if it could take your style to the next level, too? That’s where glamdocs come in. These new vendors let you customize the appearance of your cyberware, with 40 styles in different colors to choose from. Fancy a new look for your chrome? Pay them a visit at one (or all) of the five locations across Night City and see what catches your eye.

In a city that lives and dies by appearances, V really can’t afford to pass up any opportunity to shake up their look. On top of cyberware customization, we’ve also added 20 new hairstyles and several clothing sets to give your V the best chance of standing out, even in Night City.

We know how creative the Cyberpunk 2077 community can be, and we’re always curious to see what players come up with. That’s why we’re introducing cross-platform mod support through mod.io integration.

The update adds a Mods panel where you can browse and install supported community-created content directly in the game. It’s a new way to experiment with your experience, and we’re looking forward to seeing how it develops as more mods become available and receive support over time!

We’ve covered some of the bigger additions, but there’s still plenty to find in the Edgerunners 2 Update.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.title: It’s All About You! — A Crew to Remember

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.title: It’s All About You! — Never Fade Away
items.summary: Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥 Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey! Sure, th
items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
